To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the framework provides an efficient and modular solution to enable privacy-preserving NoSQL databases; (2) it supports a variety of cryptographic techniques, including homomorphic encryption and searchable symmetric encryption; and (3) it is able to process encrypted data with an average overhead in performance of 15% when compared with a baseline NoSQL database.

(1) the framework is practical for the majority of the cryptographic techniques; (2) the framework is modular, extensible and can be used to evaluate the applicability of multiple cryptographic techniques in a single database; (3) it is possible to achieve a good trade-off between privacy and performance by combining multiple cryptographic techniques in the same database; and (4) the overhead in performance is below 10% in most of the experiments, when compared with a baseline database.

(a) we provide a generic NoSQL database framework that enables data processing using multiple cryptographic techniques; (b) we provide a set of libraries to support data processing cryptographic techniques; (c) we provide an evaluation of the performance of the framework using a NoSQL engine and the YCSB workload; and (d) the average overhead in performance is below 10%.
